speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) how the new Safety Assurance for Food Establishment (SAFE) framework that will be implemented from 19 January 2026 is expected to address public health risks more effectively; and (b) what metrics does the Government plan to use in order to evaluate this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The SAFE framework is a food safety grading system that communicates food establishments’ food safety performance more clearly to consumers, so that they can make informed choices.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Under the SAFE framework, food establishments fall under two categories, based on their level of food processing or preparation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Category 1 food establishments are those with a larger scale of food processing or preparation, such as food manufacturers, caterers, central kitchens and large restaurants.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The majority of food establishments such as hawker stalls, small restaurants and bakeries fall under Category 2.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These have a smaller scale of food processing or preparation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Food establishments are graded "A", "B" or "C" based on their food safety track record from SFA’s inspections.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: They do not have to fulfil any additional requirements, unless they are Category 1 food establishments that wish to attain Grade A.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Downgraded establishments will need to build up and maintain good food safety track records, before they can move back to a higher grade.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Compared with the annual snapshot assessment under the previous grading regime, the one that we are all very familiar with, the new SAFE framework considers a food establishment’s year-round food safety track record from its history of inspections, including any involvement in food-borne incidents.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This encourages food establishments to consistently maintain good food safety practices.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: SFA will continue to conduct regular inspections of all food establishments under its targeted, data-driven regime.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Food establishments with a larger scale of food processing or preparation, as well as those with Grade C, will be inspected more frequently.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For small businesses in Category 1 that wish to implement the additional requirements and maintain their Grade A status, government support is available.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Individuals who apply for the AFHO training course will receive SkillsFuture Singapore subsidies of up to 70%.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Food businesses can send existing staff to be trained.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there is no need to hire additional staff, you can use existing staff to do this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This grant specifically supports local SMEs for their first-time certification and adoption of standards, and covers qualifying project costs such as consultancy and certification fees for FSMS standards.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Ms Nadia Samdin also asked about how the transparency and authenticity of the SAFE grades can be assured with the shift away from physical decals and how less digitally savvy consumers will be able to access information on SAFE grades.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Under the previous system, physical decals were updated annually, once a year, following inspections and they may not follow real-time changes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: By scanning the QR code on a food establishment’s licence, consumers can be assured of the most up-to-date, real-time and accurate information on the food establishment’s grade and track records.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This mitigates the risk of outdated decals being displayed at the premises.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Under the Environmental Public Health Act, food establishments must display their licence at a conspicuous and accessible position at their premises.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Consumers who are less digitally savvy or without smart devices can request the grade from the stall operator or seek assistance from a fellow diner with a smart device.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To better support such consumers, SFA has also partnered with the Infocomm Media Development Authority on the Seniors Go Digital programme to teach seniors on how to use their phone cameras to scan the SAFE QR codes at food establishments.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The first is really on the last point about accessing the food safety grading.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While I understand that the new regime will provide more up-to-date grading, I think there is also something about a physical decal making it front-and-centre for consumers to be able to consider.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, will the Ministry consider including a physical decal requirement to be updated as and when the grade may change?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My second one is, I had asked about the measurement of the effectiveness of this change in regime.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Ministry elaborate whether there will be any outcome-based indicators beyond inspection performance?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, outbreak severity or recurrence rates that will be checked alongside these compliance indicators?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My third and final one is, while SAFE strengthens assurance at the food establishment level, food safety risks can also originate earlier on in the chain – from import to processing to storage and distribution.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope to understand how SAFE fits within the broader food safety and public health architecture, if possible.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For the first one, for now, I think the critical point is to get the information out in real time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The QR code enables us to change the grading as and when one performs poorly or one has improved performance, rather than waiting once a year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But having said that, when you scan the QR code, it is part of the licence that you have to show or display.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there is a display of the licence and the QR code.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: A quick show and you can actually see whether it is a Grade A, B or C.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it is quite clear to whoever who needs to use it.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Having said that, nothing stops the outlet from also printing it themselves and pasting it up.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But we will not make it compulsory or mandatory for now, but we will see how this goes and we hope that we can educate more to use the new format.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Member's second question on the effectiveness, we will look into this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is one way in which we also want to measure effectiveness of the system as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But as it has just been launched and rolled out, give us a bit of time to assess the performance, how the ratings change.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Because we do not have enough data now to see how it changes in the new system, so, give us a bit of time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, one way in which we hope to see is to see improved performances over time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As food and beverage (F&B) outlets find that they are being monitored more in real time, they are more encouraged to keep performance up and keep food safety at a high standard.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The third question on whether we are able to trace back, down to the food source.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think we have to take a very risk-based approach.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But certainly, when there is an outbreak or when we think that there is a risk to the system, like I said, we do take a very risk-based approach especially for those who have large volume or large networks, or those have outbreaks or poor performance, and that is where we have to then assess the sources.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As part of the FSMS requirement, we will then also take a look at their records that they have to do for safekeeping.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I would also encourage F&B operators and all those licensees to really trace and track, and keep up the standards with the new grading system.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But for many Singaporeans, the real concern is whether it remains safe in practice or becomes unsafe when lapses go unnoticed.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: A heavy reliance on past track record makes oversight reactive rather than preventive.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could the Senior Minister of State explain what early warning indicators SFA uses to detect deteriorating food safety standards before a serious lapse occurs and how these safeguards protect consumers upstream rather than after harm has been done?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And secondly, in addition, what independent verification or audit measurements are in place to ensure that self-reported compliance accurately reflects on-ground practice?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I shared, our inspection regime adopts a targeted and data-driven approach.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This enables us to also track proactively, which basically means, those under the Category 1, for example, larger kitchens, those with poor track records, they will be inspected more proactively.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And of course, those who are doing better, we can do less.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And therefore, as an overall, we will not have any less inspection than we have today.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: What we want to do is to be more proactive, take a risk-based approach.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: With the gradings being monitored in real time, I think that encourages a lot of operators to monitor and ensure that they keep up their safety standards, because they are monitored in real time and whenever they have downgrades, I think there is impact.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, in some contracts in some Ministries, I also am aware that if the gradings change, they will also review the contracting requirements, the contracting conditions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are ways in which the Government also sets the standard to ensure and keep our food providers and caterers on their toes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, in terms of audit, most of the data is already with us and we already assure them by licensing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And for grading, I think that comes as part of SFA's inspections.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, when it comes to audits as example, as part of inspections, we will inspect various things, whether it is your sources, whether your AFHO certifications are in place, whether you have a pest-free environment, and so forth.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These are things in which our officers will look for which will go into your grading and risk profiling.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there is data analytics involved, in short, and we will take a risk-based approach.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: My supplementary question pertains to those establishments with poor performance, especially now that the decal is not being displayed.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: These establishments with poor performance would likely expect more frequent inspections and that means there will be disproportionately more resources on SFA's side to keep inspecting these few outlets.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: In that case, if they consistently do not perform, would SFA consider a safety time-out for these food establishments to protect the interest of consumers, especially if the decal is not even displayed and most people would not take the trouble to check, so how would they know that these are the frequent ones that do not improve?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Food safety and hygiene is top priority and top of mind for us.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, rest assured that there are measures under our food safety regulations and the Food Safety and Security Act to ensure that we maintain high food standards here in Singapore and for all our consumers.
